frames.narration: A pull request changes a support prompt. CI asks the platform to compare it with the baseline on dataset v12, a pinned, scrubbed set of 2,000 cases, with a regression budget of 2 points. The scheduler first estimates the cost: about 4,000 model calls (2,000 candidate answers and up to 2,000 judge calls), within the team's budget.

The baseline outputs for this dataset and these pinned settings are already in the cache from an earlier run, so only the candidate needs to be run: 2,000 tasks, each keyed by run, case and repeat so a retry never duplicates a result.

Workers take tasks through a token-bucket limiter that holds this team to its share of the provider's quota. When the provider answers 429, the worker waits as the retry-after header says, with a little jitter. The run finishes in about 10 minutes.

The graders run deterministic checks first (valid JSON, citation present, length), then a calibrated judge for the quality rubric on cases that passed the checks. The judge's answer is validated, and the text being graded is quoted as data.

The comparison is paired. Baseline passes 1,400 of 2,000 cases (70.0%), the candidate 1,460 (73.0%). It fixed 150 cases and broke 90, so 60 more pass. A bootstrap of the paired differences gives +1.5 to +4.5 points.

The lower end, +1.5, is above the regression budget of minus 2, so the check passes. It is also above zero, so the improvement is real, not noise. Slice results are posted too, and a drop in one rare language is flagged for a person to look at, not blocked.

The run manifest is stored with the results: dataset hash, prompt and judge versions, model snapshot, settings, seed and commit. After the change is released, the online monitor grades 1% of live traces with the same graders and compares them with this result.

Weeks later the questions change: a new product launch brings topics that dataset v12 does not cover. The online pass rate on that slice falls below the interval from the offline run, and the monitor alerts the team, who add the new traces to dataset v13.
